Accuracy first, speed second. The fast fingers come later.
Every typo is a small lesson. Notice which key betrayed you, slow down for a moment, and let the rhythm come back on its own.
Keep your eyes on the text, not on your hands. Your fingers already know where the keys are, so trust them and let your focus stay one word ahead.
A steady pace beats a frantic one. Type at the speed where you make almost no mistakes, and the numbers will climb without any extra effort.

Touch typing is a skill built from tiny repetitions. Each lesson adds a few keys, each session smooths the rough edges, and after enough quiet practice your hands move faster than you can think about them. There is no shortcut, only the pleasant habit of coming back tomorrow.

The home row is the anchor. Your index fingers rest on the small bumps of the F and J keys, and every other finger stays curled nearby, ready to reach out and return. Always come home after a reach, and the whole keyboard will start to feel small.

When you practice, choose accuracy over speed for the first few minutes. Errors teach your fingers the wrong path, and unlearning is slower than learning. Build the clean habit first, then let the pace rise gently until it reaches the edge of your comfort.
